successors.name: Kalabhra dynasty
successors.text: the Chera country of central Kerala and the Kongu country; 'The Kalabhras rose in the region'

ledger.x: c. 180: the Chera kingdom reaches Kongu. Chenguttuvan 'c. 180 CE' (the page says 'either the first or the last quarter of the second century CE'): 'Chera territory covered the Malabar Coast and the Kongu country'; the capital Vanchi-Karuvur (Karur) lies there. The page does not say the land was gained then, nor from…

c. 305: the Early Cheras end in Cliopatria. The Chera page is silent: it gives 'between the third and fifth centuries CE' for a decline and 'c. 5th century CE' for the end. The Kalabhra page says they ruled 'sometime between the 3rd century and 6th century CE' (earliest inscription 270 CE) after 'the ancient dynasties…

certainty.note: No Chera frontier is recorded on the pages; the page describes territory only by regions (Malabar Coast, Kongu country, Palakkad Gap).
